page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne-c8d3.8xlarge is a big data-focused virtual machine instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 16-core, 32-thread Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory configuration includes 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance features a 20 Gbps baseline network throughput and includes a substantial 70,866 GB local HDD storage array, without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluation reveals solid parallel processing alongside modest per-core performance. Single-core tests reflect lower-tier per-thread execution, placing in the bottom quartile with a Geekbench single-core score of 965.0 and weak single-threaded compression speeds. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics remain firmly in the median range, registering 23,516.82 on stress-ng multi-core tests, a PassMark CPU score of 22,938.9, and 22.28 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 65.79 GB/s.

Architectural tradeoffs balance massive local storage density against mechanical drive access latencies and moderate single-thread compute capabilities. While the high HDD capacity offers favorable storage volume per resource unit, it is not engineered for random I/O-intensive database workloads requiring solid-state performance. The instance is suited for batch processing, distributed storage clusters such as Hadoop Distributed File System, data warehousing, and log collection pipelines that process high volumes of sequential data.

Designed for storage-dense workloads, the system incorporates an integrated 70,866 GB local HDD volume and a 20 Gbps baseline network interface, while omitting GPU acceleration. Benchmark assessments demonstrate moderate multi-core throughput, recording a PassMark CPU score of 22,938.9 and 22.28 million Redis SET operations per second, contrasted by lower-tier single-core efficiency as evidenced by a 965.0 Geekbench single-core score. Memory bandwidth reaches 65.79 GB/s for uncached reads. The hardware profile creates a distinct operational tradeoff, emphasizing massive sequential storage capacity over high single-threaded speed or low-latency solid-state storage. Consequently, the instance is structured primarily for large-scale sequential data operations, including distributed big data frameworks, Hadoop analytics, large log aggregations, and batch ETL processing.
